summary: Small owners hit by higher tariffs on supplies chose different answers: cut part-time helpers, shrink the line, or hold prices and take less.
realLife: NBC News described small businesses after tariffs raised their costs. A pottery owner said a supplier added 7.25 percent and she would rather close than raise prices. A custom apparel pair cut part-time high school helpers who earned $12 to $15 an hour and delayed a storefront. A soap maker planned to cut varieties and swap oils to hold her price. A toy maker switched suppliers and said nothing would make him raise prices. An awards business with six workers faced 20 percent supplier increases and expected to raise prices.
sources: https://www.nbcnews.com/business/business-news/small-businesses-are-swearing-tariff-price-hikes-costing-rcna205395 (NBC News on small owners and tariff costs)
